title: King Moggallana I
biography: Moggallana I (495–512 CE) reclaimed the throne from his brother Kashyapa I after defeating him in battle. His 17-year reign focused on restoring Anuradhapura as the capital, abandoning Sigiriya's fortress isolation. He emphasized Buddhist reconciliation, sponsoring monastic communities and reinforcing orthodox Theravāda practices. His rule sought to legitimize his succession through piety and administrative normalization, distancing his reign from Kashyapa's parricide stigma.

title: Pachacuti Inca Yupanqui (Earth Shaker)
biography: Founder of the Inca Empire who transformed the small Kingdom of Cusco into the vast empire of Tawantinsuyu. Rebuilt Cusco in the shape of a puma, constructed the Sacsayhuaman megalithic fortress, and built the mountaintop royal estate of Machu Picchu.
internationalConnections: Constructed the Qhapaq Ñan imperial highway system spanning thousands of miles across Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, and Argentina.

title: King Siri Sangha Bodhi II
biography: Siri Sangha Bodhi II (797–801 CE) governed briefly for four years. His reign maintained hydraulic and religious infrastructure amid late 8th-century transitions. Limited narrative detail implies effective routine governance without dramatic reforms.

title: King Jayabahu II
biography: Jayabahu II's brief five-year reign followed his father Parakramabahu VI. He maintained Buddhist ceremonies and Kotte's administrative framework, but lacked the predecessor's unifying force. His short tenure foreshadowed the kingdom's fragmentation into rival principalities.

title: King Kasi Nayinar Cinkaiariyan
biography: Kasi Nayinar Cinkaiariyan was installed by the Portuguese after his predecessor's overthrow, ruling Jaffna as a client for five years. He maintained Hindu ceremonies under Portuguese supervision, but his reign represented a sharp loss of autonomy for the northern kingdom.

title: King Rajasinha I
biography: Rajasinha I (1581–1593) succeeded Mayadunne in Sitawaka, ruling for twelve years with fierce anti-Portuguese militancy. He conquered Kotte temporarily, besieged Portuguese forts, and attempted to eliminate Christian influence. However, internal overextension and succession disputes weakened Sitawaka; after his death, the kingdom collapsed. His reign represents the zenith and denouement of militant Sinhalese resistance based in Sitawaka.

internationalConnections: Rajasinha I of Sitawaka waged relentless war against the Portuguese for 12 years, nearly driving them from the island. He besieged Colombo and forced Kotte into submission, but internal strife and Portuguese naval superiority prevented total victory.
